course_title: Physiotherapy Specialties: Musculoskeletal IIB (Cervical and Thoracic Spine)
course_description:
This course will provide students with knowledge and understanding of the musculoskeletal pathologies of the cervical and thoracic spines and craniomandibular region, the physical manifestations of cervical, thoracic and upper quadrant disorders, differentiation of cervical versus other origins of condition such as headache, dizziness and face pain, the clinical reasoning process in clinical assessment and diagnosis, physiotherapy treatment options, rationales and treatment selection.

This courseﾠprepares students toﾠmanage patients with neck disorders and deals with the prevention of neck pain, using a biopsychosocial approach informed by the latest research evidence base. The course will provide students with knowledge and understanding of the musculoskeletal pathologies of the cervical and thoracic spines and craniomandibular region, the physical manifestations of cervical, thoracic and upper quadrant disorders, differentiation of cervical versus other origins of conditions such as headache, dizziness and face pain, the clinical reasoning process in clinical assessment and diagnosis of the patient with a neck disorder, physiotherapy treatment options, rationales and treatment selection.ﾠThe course includes theoretical and practical information, including biomechanical analyses of static and dynamic postures of the upper quadrant, cervical and thoracic segmental joint examination, examination of the nervous system, muscle and motor controlﾠfor the cervical and thoracic spines and craniomandibular systems.ﾠIn addition, the specific needs of specialty areas in sport, overuse, sub-optimal functional use, as well as inflammatory and degenerative conditions will be explored, as will behavioural featuresﾠassociated with cervical pain. Students will develop the communication and practical skills needed to competently assess and safely and effectively treat clients with cervical, thoracic and craniomandibular disorders, to predict and evaluate outcomes as well as develop programs for promotion of good musculoskeletal health for the prevention of injury or the prevention of recurrence of injury to the cervical and thoracic spines.ﾠThe multidisciplinary nature of care of disorders will be discussed and the physiotherapist’s role and responsibilities in the health care team will be explored.

course_aims:
The purpose of the course is to develop the student’s knowledge, attributes and skills in:

1. Researching, identifying and describing pathological conditions of the cervical, thoracic and craniomandibular regions.

2. Performing a comprehensive physiotherapy assessment of a clinical presentation of the cervical, thoracic and craniomandibular regions.

3. Developing communication skills for effective interaction with clients, families and other health professionals and for communication with government, health insurance and legal professions.

4. Developing clinical reasoning skills involving interpretation and analysis of assessment findings necessary for effective assessment and treatment of cervical, thoracic and craniomandibular conditions.

5. Differential diagnosis of cervical, thoracic and craniomandibular conditions to identify those requiring multiprofessional management orﾠthose arising from other causes not relevant to physiotherapy management.

6. Applying specific practical techniques in the areas of musculoskeletal physiotherapy and specficﾠexercise prescription used in the management of cervical, thoracic and craniomandibular disorders, as well as the prevention of injury and reinjury.

7. Understanding and working in an evidence based framework of health care, accountability and responsibility to the client and the health care team.

8. Developing the necessary skills for life long learning, critical appraisal of new management methods and the judegment to incorporate new research based practices into physiotherapy management plans.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify, describe, and critically appraise evidence on pathological conditions of the cervical, thoracic, and craniomandibular musculoskeletal and sensorimotor systems.
Explain and apply clinical reasoning principles in the physiotherapy management of cervical, thoracic, and craniomandibular disorders.
Perform a comprehensive, effective, culturally safe physiotherapy assessment of a cervical, thoracic spine and craniomandibular musculoskeletal clinical presentation.
Identify conditions that require interprofessional management or are outside the scope of physiotherapy, and identify appropriate referral pathways.
Demonstrate effective, tailored communication skills that meet the needs of clients, families, and other health professionals, as well as government, health insurance and legal bodies.
Safely and proficiently apply manual techniques and targeted exercise programs to manage and prevent upper quadrant musculoskeletal disorders.
Demonstrate accountability and professional responsibility in physiotherapy practice through the application of evidence-based healthcare.
Critically appraise physiotherapy management approaches and demonstrate the ability to integrate new evidence into clinical decision-making and ongoing professional development.
